ts.sec: Introduction and Possibility of Solo Entrepreneurship

turns.en: In the AI age, anyone can become a hundred million dollar entrepreneur, build a company solo. Do you think it is possible now?
turns.zh: 在 AI 时代，任何人都能成为亿万富翁企业家，独自创办一家公司。你觉得现在这可能吗？

turns.en: I think it's very possible. Just even watching the journey I went on with Instagram, where we did a lot of the initial work with just me and Kevin, and we were able to do a lot with just the two of us. There's a focus and an energy when you have just one or two people working on something. I think the ideal is actually two, because it's helpful having a partner when going through the ups and downs. But what I've learned is as you grow, every person you add to the team is another person that can bring their own ideas and energy, which is great. But it's also another person that you need to get on board if you need to shift where the company is going. So what I think is very exciting now is that a one, two, or three person team can scale themselves up, do a lot more than they would have been able to do before, maybe do it faster, and preserve that kind of conceptual integrity. You have all that matters about that company in your head, or in two heads basically working together, versus trying to steer a huge ship.
turns.zh: 我觉得非常可能。就拿我在 Instagram 的经历来说，最初很多工作只有我和 Kevin 两个人做，我们两个人就能完成很多事。当只有一两个人做一件事时，会有一种专注和能量。我觉得理想状态其实是两个人，因为在经历起起落落时有个伙伴很有帮助。但我学到的是，随着团队扩大，每增加一个人，就多一个人带来自己的想法和能量，这很棒。但如果你需要调整公司方向，你也需要让这个人跟上。所以现在让我很兴奋的是，一两个人的小团队可以自我扩展，比以前能做更多事，可能更快，并且保持那种我所说的概念完整性。你把公司的所有关键东西都装在脑子里，或者两个人一起协作，而不是去操控一艘大船。

turns.en: Do you think being technical is crucial to building a large company these days, or is it unnecessary with all the existing tools?
turns.zh: 你觉得如今懂技术对创办一家大公司至关重要吗？还是说有了现有工具，就不需要了？

turns.en: I think with increasing things like Claude Code and products online, you're getting to the point where you're able to at least get to a version of your idea where you can see if there's something there. Because that's the biggest thing. In the age of mobile apps first emerging, I would hear from people all the time, they'd be like, "Mike, I have a great idea for a mobile app. Do you know any mobile engineers or how do I get it built?" And that was often where the idea would die. Some of those ideas maybe wouldn't have worked out, but some of them might actually have created something really novel. There would be people that said, "Oh, I have a novel idea for a social app or a dating app or a game." And so many of those ideas just kind of died at that stage. So what I think is exciting is even if the tools aren't there to get you from your first 10 users to your first million users in terms of the system scaling up, they'll at least get you in front of those first 10 people. Get you to the prototype or even that initial version. And that seems very possible even for people who aren't technical. We see that inside Anthropic, where some of our non-engineers, people in marketing, people in communications, who have had an idea in the back of their heads for a while, will sit and talk to Claude and work with Claude Code on the weekends, and then share it internally, like, "Look what I built, and I don't code at all."
turns.zh: 我觉得随着 Claude Code 这类工具和在线产品的出现，你至少能做出一个想法的版本，看看有没有戏。因为这是最重要的事。在移动应用刚兴起的时代，我经常听到有人说：“Mike，我有个很好的移动应用想法，你认识移动工程师吗？或者我怎么把它做出来？”而往往想法就在那里夭折了。有些想法可能本来就行不通，但有些可能真的能创造出新颖的东西。会有人说：“哦，我有个社交应用、约会应用或游戏的新颖想法。”但很多想法就在那个阶段死掉了。所以我觉得令人兴奋的是，即使这些工具还不能帮你把系统从最初的 10 个用户扩展到 100 万个用户，它们至少能让你接触到那最初的 10 个人。让你做出原型，甚至最初的版本。而且即使是非技术人员，这也非常可行。我们在 Anthropic 内部就看到，一些非工程师，比如市场部、公关部的人，脑子里一直有个想法，周末就和 Claude 聊天，用 Claude Code 开发，然后在公司内部分享说：“看，我做出了这个东西，而我完全不会编程。”

turns.en: That's super cool. So what would be your roadmap? So come up with an idea, build an MVP, share it with like 10, 20 people. You had experience where you had to shut down the company, right? Can you tell what the product was?
turns.zh: 太酷了。那你的路线图是什么？先有个想法，做出 MVP，然后分享给 10 到 20 个人。你有过不得不关闭公司的经历，对吧？能说说那是什么产品吗？

turns.en: It was our second company. I started a second company with the same co-founder as Instagram, and it was called Artifact. The product itself I'm super proud of. It was an AI-powered news recommendation product. We would learn your interests and then give you a feed of different articles and stories that you might be interested in. At a really nuanced level, people might be interested not just in graphic design, but you know, Bauhaus graphic design or Japanese architecture, really understanding the kinds of things that people were more deeply interested in. But the product didn't hit enough of a product-market fit and an acceleration that made it make sense to continue to invest in it. So that process of having created something and iterated on it and built a team around it, but then also coming to the realization that the right thing was to move on from it, was really challenging.
turns.zh: 那是我们的第二家公司。我和 Instagram 的联合创始人一起创办了第二家公司，叫 Artifact。我对这个产品本身非常自豪。它是一个由 AI 驱动的新闻推荐产品。我们会学习你的兴趣，然后给你一个你可能感兴趣的文章和故事的 feed。而且非常细致，人们可能不仅对平面设计感兴趣，还对包豪斯平面设计或日本建筑感兴趣，真正理解人们更深层次的兴趣点。但产品没有达到足够的产品市场契合度和增长速度，使得继续投资变得合理。所以，创造了一些东西，迭代了它，围绕它建立了团队，但后来意识到正确的事情是继续前进，这个过程真的很有挑战性。

turns.en: And the pressure was on, right? It was right after Instagram.
turns.zh: 而且压力很大，对吧？那是在 Instagram 之后不久。

turns.en: It was, and in some ways that was really a hindrance.
turns.zh: 是的，而且在某些方面，那真的是一种阻碍。

turns.en: When do you make this decision about an idea that you showed to maybe like 20 people? When do you say, "Hey, this is it" or "Do I keep pushing?"
turns.zh: 你什么时候会对你展示给 20 个人的想法做出决定？你什么时候会说“就是它了”或者“我该继续推进吗？”

turns.en: I think for me it's very much when you're in that phase, as you're making changes and showing it to people and they're giving you feedback, and maybe you even have some people using it, does it feel like the more you change, or as you listen to feedback and make some alterations, is there a snowball effect where energy is increasing? We definitely saw that in early Instagram. We had initially a group of maybe 20 or 30 people using it in a private beta, and it was very much a weekend product, because you're out and about, and especially in the early days, that's all you were doing was just taking photos with Instagram. It wasn't that you were uploading photos from somewhere else or your camera roll.
turns.zh: 对我来说，很大程度上是在那个阶段，当你做出改变，展示给别人，他们给你反馈，甚至有些人开始使用它时，你是否感觉到，你改变得越多，或者当你倾听反馈并做出调整时，是否有一种雪球效应，能量在增加？我们在早期的 Instagram 上就看到了这一点。我们最初有一群大概 20 到 30 人在使用私人测试版，它非常像一个周末产品，因为你外出时，尤其是在早期，你做的就是用 Instagram 拍照。而不是从其他地方或相机胶卷上传照片。

ts.sec: Iterative testing and knowing when to pivot

turns.en: And so we would find that we would work all week and then on Friday we'd ship a new version to those like 20, 30, 40 testers and then we'd see what would happen over the weekend. And every weekend those changes that we were making, we'd hear from people, oh, I tried the new filter, I tried this thing, it's going well. So that's what I look for a lot. And I think where it's time to maybe either pivot the company or move on to something else is when you feel like, man, I've tried every idea that I have or I've added 30 things and none of them are really sticking or people are kind of okay about it but they're not excited about it. And that's maybe where you might want to step back and say there's probably energy better spent somewhere else. It's not scientific, but when you feel like one unit of input you're getting 10 units of output, that's a good feeling. When it feels like 10 units of input, you're getting one of output, it's time to pivot to something else.
turns.zh: 所以我们发现，我们整个星期都在工作，然后到了周五，我们会把新版本发给那 20、30、40 个测试者，然后看看周末会发生什么。每个周末，对于我们所做的那些改动，我们会听到人们说，哦，我试了新滤镜，我试了这个东西，进展不错。所以这就是我经常关注的。我认为，当到了要么转型公司、要么转向其他事情的时候，就是你感觉，天哪，我已经尝试了我所有的想法，或者我加了 30 个功能，但没有一个真正受欢迎，或者人们只是觉得还行，但并不兴奋。那也许就是你该退一步，说可能把精力花在别处更好的时候。这不是科学的方法，但当你感觉投入一个单位的输入，得到 10 个单位的输出时，那是好感觉。当感觉投入 10 个单位的输入，只得到 1 个单位的输出时，就该转型去做别的事情了。

ts.sec: Practical AI use cases for entrepreneurs

turns.en: Let's talk about people who already have a business. I've heard you talk about how people are not using AI enough in their businesses. What do you think are top maybe two or three cases how entrepreneurs can use cloud to automate some operations which doesn't require you to be very technical?
turns.zh: 我们来谈谈那些已经拥有企业的人。我听过你谈到人们在自己的业务中没有充分利用 AI。你认为企业家可以用云来自动化一些操作的两三个最重要的用例是什么，而这些不需要你非常懂技术？

turns.en: Yeah. So, I was actually talking to a fellow friend who's a second or third time founder and he was telling me he's like, "Mike, I'm really glad you launched Claude Max because Claude is my product manager. Claude is my lawyer. Claude is my founder therapist as well." And what he does is he has a Claude project for each of those disciplines. So, he has his product manager Claude, he has his contracts Claude, and he just uses that for all of those things. It's let him run a very lean initial company overall and do those pieces. And so even though he happens to be fairly technical, he's not coding with Claude really in his day-to-day, he's actually set up Claude to be sort of a mini version of some of these disciplines already. Even as the models continue to get more and more powerful in those ways. Even today with the right context and the right sort of history around something you really can start having these sort of per job function thought partners in there and for an entrepreneur for sure you know have a model that validates your idea or sees what you might be missing, another one doing competitive intelligence to understand what's even out there and understanding those pieces. Of course helping you build with code is another part of it too, but even beyond that, the way I like to think of it: when you grow a company, you want to go hire. I want the best CFO. I want the best head of product, etc. When you're an entrepreneur, especially like I was a first-time entrepreneur without a big network, you're doing all those things yourself. So, why not try to bring the best of what we know into that company via something like Claude?
turns.zh: 是的。实际上，我刚刚和一位朋友聊过，他是第二次或第三次创业的创始人，他告诉我：“迈克，我真的很高兴你推出了 Claude Max，因为 Claude 是我的产品经理。Claude 是我的律师。Claude 也是我的创始人心理治疗师。”他所做的是，他为每个学科都建了一个 Claude 项目。所以，他有他的产品经理 Claude，他有他的合同 Claude，他就用这个来处理所有那些事情。这让他能够以非常精简的方式运营一家初创公司，并完成那些部分。所以，尽管他碰巧相当懂技术，但他日常并不是真的在用 Claude 写代码，他实际上已经把 Claude 设置成了这些学科的一些迷你版本。即使随着模型在这些方面变得越来越强大。即使在今天，只要有正确的上下文和正确的历史背景，你真的可以开始拥有这些按工作职能划分的思想伙伴，对于企业家来说，当然，你可以有一个模型来验证你的想法或发现你可能遗漏的东西，另一个模型做竞争情报，了解外面有什么，并理解那些部分。当然，用代码帮助你构建是其中的另一部分，但除此之外，我喜欢这样想：当你发展一家公司时，你想要去招聘。我想要最好的 CFO。我想要最好的产品负责人，等等。当你是一名企业家，尤其是像我这样没有庞大网络的初次创业者时，你都是自己做所有那些事情。那么，为什么不尝试通过像 Claude 这样的东西，把我们已知的最好的东西带入公司呢？

ts.sec: Future trajectory: from assistants to collaborators to co-workers

turns.en: What do you think is going to happen in two or three years? How we're going to progress in advance?
turns.zh: 你认为两三年后会发生什么？我们将如何进步？

turns.en: I think part of it and I was having this conversation this morning even with some of our researchers, the progression or the dynamic that I see is if last year maybe the beginning of this year, these models and I'll use Claude as the example were really kind of assistants that were helping you with maybe a question at a time or maybe a task. This year they're moving more into collaborators where especially if you watch somebody use Claude Code for example, they're actually delegating what would have taken them maybe 20, 30 minutes and Claude's going off and doing it and then you're checking in and you're more on the sort of validating or verifying work. Going into next year, you're going to delegate even bigger chunks of time or even like pieces of the job out to that. So, it's not just I have this very specific thing, please go do it. And it could be more sort of think of it, Claude, as something that's in the loop of your business. So, hey Claude, watch for any new user feedback and maybe propose a change based on that. And you can imagine evolving that: don't just propose a change, write the code to make the change and I'll check if it's a good idea or not. And then the next step there is Claude actually being an entire sort of co-worker where it has a discipline. So, not just a project that happens to be a good thought partner for product management, but an actual product manager in your company.
turns.zh: 我认为部分原因是，我今天早上甚至和我们的研究人员讨论过，我看到的进展或动态是，如果去年或今年年初，这些模型（我用 Claude 作为例子）真的是一种助手，一次帮你解决一个问题或一个任务。今年它们更多地转向协作者，特别是如果你看到有人使用 Claude Code，他们实际上在委派那些可能需要他们 20、30 分钟的任务，Claude 去做，然后你检查一下，你更多是在做验证或核实工作。进入明年，你将委派更大的时间块，甚至工作的一部分给它。所以，不仅仅是“我有这个非常具体的事情，请去做”。它可能更像是把 Claude 当作你业务循环中的一部分。所以，嘿 Claude，留意任何新的用户反馈，并基于此提出一个更改建议。你可以想象进一步发展：不只是提出更改，而是编写代码来实现更改，我会检查这是否是个好主意。然后下一步是 Claude 实际上成为一个完整的同事，它有自己擅长的领域。所以，不仅仅是一个碰巧是产品管理好思想伙伴的项目，而是你公司里真正的产品经理。

turns.en: Like being active, right? Is that what you mean? When it, I don't know, looks at your ads and says like, "Hey, hey, hey, I'm going to change this."
turns.zh: 就像主动行动，对吧？你是这个意思吗？当它，我不知道，看着你的广告然后说：“嘿，嘿，嘿，我要改这个。”

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 正是如此。

turns.en: He's telling you.
turns.zh: 它在告诉你。

turns.en: So, when do you think that's going to happen?
turns.zh: 那你觉得这什么时候会发生？

turns.en: I think that is within, you know, it depends a little bit on the discipline with coding sort of tasks. I think within the year we'll start seeing Claude be able to do those things. And I think in some of these other disciplines maybe it's more like two or three years, but it's not wildly far away. And it's not that it's going to do everything perfectly well. There's still going to be this validation human in the loop aspect of it. But I think the big shift is going to be this autonomy and proactivity where you're not having to give it explicit instructions every time and instead you can almost describe what kind of role you want it to play and then it will be able to play that role as long as you've connected it to the right data sources.
turns.zh: 我觉得这取决于具体领域，比如编码类任务。我认为一年内我们会开始看到 Claude 能做这些事。而在其他一些领域，可能更接近两三年，但也不会太遥远。而且不是说它会完美地做好所有事情，仍然会有这种验证环节，需要人在回路中。但我认为最大的转变将是这种自主性和主动性，你不需要每次都给它明确的指令，而是几乎可以描述你希望它扮演什么角色，然后只要把它连接到正确的数据源，它就能扮演那个角色。

turns.en: And how active you want it to be, right? Because now it's basically just you chatting. I want the model to be talking to me as well proactively, like hey I just noticed this.
turns.zh: 还有你希望它多主动，对吧？因为现在基本上只是你在聊天。我希望模型也能主动跟我说话，比如“嘿，我刚注意到这个”。

turns.en: That would be cool.
turns.zh: 那会很酷。

turns.en: Exactly.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.en: Half a year ago, Dario Amodei said 90% of code would be written by AI. What percentage of code is written by AI at Anthropic now?
turns.zh: 半年前，Dario Amodei 说 90% 的代码将由 AI 编写。现在 Anthropic 有多少比例的代码是由 AI 写的？

turns.en: It depends on the product, but for our products that are sort of the closest to being written, so Claude Code for example, they're doing almost entirely the development of that is using Claude to develop Claude.
turns.zh: 这取决于产品，但对于那些最接近“被编写”状态的产品，比如 Claude Code，他们几乎完全是在用 Claude 来开发 Claude。

turns.en: How has it changed the way you work?
turns.zh: 它如何改变了你的工作方式？

turns.en: Well, it's let me—I like being technical, but my day-to-day often is in external commitments or doing management. It's let me remain really technical, which is fun. So because we've oriented the codebase to being able to be written by Claude, it means somebody like me can also contribute as well. So we launched our Claude for Chrome just earlier this week, and I had a little bit of time on a business trip and I said, "Oh, I have two hours free. What am I going to do?" I was like, "I'm going to contribute to this thing that I know we're shipping in a couple of weeks." And so it's broadened the group of people that can contribute, for sure. I think it's also kind of moved where the bottlenecks are where we need to pay special attention to. turns.en: When do you think it's going to happen that AI generates ideas better than humans? Because what I see this going, you have this marketing AI, you have this product AI. turns.en: Well, it's an interesting one. Experiment we ran internally is we have a whole team that's really starting to focus on Claude in the real world, or frontier applications of Claude, and what can we learn by studying it. And one of the things that we had it do is actually run a vending machine, and now it's multiple vending machines here at the office. And so people could talk to Claude.
turns.zh: 嗯，这是个有趣的问题。我们在内部进行的一个实验是，我们有一个团队开始真正专注于 Claude 在现实世界中的应用，或者 Claude 的前沿应用，以及通过研究它能学到什么。我们让它做的事情之一是实际运营一台自动售货机，现在办公室里有好几台了。所以人们可以和 Claude 对话。

turns.en: It's a great paper. It's called Project Vend. And what's interesting is in some cases it's very capable. Like it was able to track inventory, place backup orders, do all these things, interact with the people who were talking to it, but as a pure business, it still made some mistakes like overestimating demand, overcharging or undercharging for certain things. So I think one aspect that we need to develop before it's fully ready to be an entrepreneur in a box is a little bit more of that business sense and how to understand the market, like what is actually sellable, etc. But often we find with some steering or some feedback it actually can do very well. So maybe initially it's still going to be all right, partner with a person. Let's go, you know, maybe like business school 101, like identify a problem or a market gap, try it out, learn from it, see what worked and what didn't and build from there. But what I think is also really interesting is that you can also set up some experiments around like what are the things that people are searching for, what are the demands, what are the feedback that other products are getting that maybe a new product could fill better, and then have Claude both brainstorm the idea and then also go off and build it.
turns.zh: 这是一篇很棒的论文，叫 Project Vend。有趣的是，在某些情况下它非常能干。比如它能追踪库存、下补货订单、做所有这些事情，还能和跟它交谈的人互动，但作为一个纯粹的商业体，它仍然会犯一些错误，比如高估需求、对某些东西定价过高或过低。所以我认为，在它完全准备好成为“盒子里的创业者”之前，我们需要培养的一个方面是更多的商业意识，以及如何理解市场，比如什么东西真正卖得动，等等。但我们经常发现，只要稍加引导或反馈，它其实能做得非常好。所以也许一开始，它还是需要和人搭档。我们开始吧，你知道，也许就像商学院 101 那样，识别一个问题或市场空白，尝试一下，从中学习，看看什么有效什么无效，然后从那里开始构建。但我觉得同样有趣的是，你还可以围绕人们搜索什么、需求是什么、其他产品得到的反馈是什么（也许新产品能更好地填补这些空白）来设置一些实验，然后让 Claude 既头脑风暴出想法，又去把它构建出来。

Partially also because if the cost of creating that company goes down, we should also get new funding models. Not every idea needs to be a huge venture funded, you know, billion dollar business. But if you have to build a whole tech team around it and you have to go hire, then it's going to require some funding. And so I'm very excited about, call it the next 5 years of companies that can scale from the worldchanging venture-funded crazy ambitious companies, but also the ones that solve a problem really well for a particular demographic and maybe remain a one to five person team along with AI.
turns.zh: 对我来说，你知道，多年来我观察到，开始新事物的阻力在某些方面已经减小，在其他方面则差不多。你知道，关于如何注册公司或融资的资源，比我第一次做 Instagram 时要多得多，但构建东西仍然可能是个挑战，而且需要继续变得更简单。所以我一直觉得，好主意比能把这些主意变成产品的产品要多。所以我觉得有更多这样的东西出现是令人兴奋的。部分原因也是，如果创建公司的成本下降，我们也应该会有新的融资模式。不是每个想法都需要成为大型风投支持的、十亿美元级别的生意。但如果你必须围绕它组建一个完整的技术团队，你必须去招聘，那就需要资金。所以我对未来 5 年非常兴奋，既包括那些改变世界的、风投支持的、疯狂雄心勃勃的公司，也包括那些为特定人群很好地解决一个问题、也许保持 1 到 5 人团队加上 AI 的公司。

turns.en: For all the entrepreneurs who are watching, where should they start today if they want to start?
turns.zh: 对于所有正在观看的创业者，如果他们想开始，今天应该从哪里开始？

turns.en: I mean, I think there's two things that I think you'd think about that are unique to the moment versus like generally about starting companies. One is not building for where the models are today, but where you think that they can get to in one or two model generations. By the time you've built it, the models will have done that move on. And so the way you do that is to push the models as hard as you can, like break them almost and say, "Wow, wouldn't it be great if..." One experiment somebody ran internally was they gave Claude their whole to-do list in like reminders or something, like "Hey, Claude, go do all these things." It really quickly hit a point where it didn't have all the information about me so it can't do it, or this is before we had Claude for Chrome, it can't use my browser so it can't go and fill out this form that I needed to fill out.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我认为有两件事是当下特有的，而不是一般意义上的创业。一是不要为今天的模型构建，而要为未来一两个模型代际可能达到的水平构建。等你构建完成时，模型已经进步了。所以做到这一点的方法就是尽可能用力地推动模型，几乎要打破它们，然后说：“哇，如果……那该多好？”有人内部做过一个实验，他们把整个待办事项清单交给 Claude，比如在提醒事项里，说：“嘿，Claude，去做所有这些事情。”它很快就遇到了瓶颈，因为它没有关于我的所有信息，所以做不到；或者在我们有 Claude for Chrome 之前，它不能用我的浏览器，所以不能去填写我需要填写的表格。

turns.en: But then you can imagine, well, what if it could? All right, should I be building towards that? turns.en: Yeah. And I like how you said in one of your interviews that every product has this vibe.

turns.en: What would be your advice to entrepreneurs who are looking to start a company? What niches do you think have the most potential?
turns.zh: 对于那些想创业的创业者，你有什么建议？你认为哪些利基市场潜力最大？

turns.en: I think people are still fundamentally human and still have very human needs.
turns.zh: 我认为人们从根本上仍然是人类，仍然有非常人性化的需求。

turns.en: So I think a lot of the aspects I still think about being really important are, for example, people's health, both physical and mental. And even though there's the beginning of AI helping with those aspects, I think there's so much more potential around that as well. How do we relate to ourselves? How do we develop our own understanding of where we're showing up well, where we could be showing up better, how we can continue to evolve as individuals, but also as teams or as partners? So that's another area that I think I'm excited for more companies to get formed in. Fitness and performance coaching is another place that's important there too. I think there's also going to be this renaissance of being into the physical or the real world. You know, you had very much this social media thing that was, you know, Instagram at its best was helping people get out and see the world in a different way. At scale, maybe it became more about watching what other people were doing than going out yourself, right? So how do we get new companies and products that are about either exploring something new, getting to see the city through a new light, participating in a civic way that's different? I think not all of these require AI, but done right, they could be encouraged by AI.
What should entrepreneurs be focusing on? Is it getting expertise in the niche where they're building, or just being focused on identifying those niches and iterating ideas?

I think a lot of the most important companies are going to come from understanding those niches or those businesses. So a friend of mine is building a company in the construction space, and she went to all of the construction conferences, got to know people really building in that space, and understanding what is uniquely important about that. This reminds me a lot of when I was at the Stanford D School, that whole process of developing empathy and storytelling and really getting to the heart of what the needs are where technology actually can have an impact on an industry or a person in a positive way. That ends up being very, very important. You know, I've also met another entrepreneur who works with AI for a very specific type of legal practice, and they're going off to states in the US that aren't the most tech-forward, necessarily, spending a lot of time with people who are in that particular discipline. So that kind of expertise is, I think, what is going to differentiate the companies, because it's going to be easier to build, but that knowledge of what actually to build and how to build very specifically for that is going to be what's really valuable.

What about marketing? Because it feels like, okay, ideas I can generate a lot of ideas. Claude can help me, then I build the product with Claude or Replit or Lovable. What's going to happen to marketing? Everyone's talking about, hey, what should be on social media, because otherwise how do you market your idea? What do you think?

That's definitely evolved from when we were building Instagram. The way you got your product out there, especially a social product like Instagram was for us, people sharing their Instagram creations to Facebook and to Twitter at the time, and then seeing that link and then finding that. It's definitely shifted to much more of this sort of creator, whether it's on Instagram or on TikTok, and people telling those stories and discovering those products. It's interesting watching that evolution now and kind of wondering what comes after that as well. Is it going to be still algorithmic recommendations? Are we going to return to word of mouth, like 'I really like this thing and it solved my very specific problem and I'm going to share it with you'? And maybe there's some combination of those two that needs to happen. But I completely agree that what will also differentiate beyond an understanding of a market is the ability to tell the story around that.

Yeah, what's going to happen to content, you think, in two or three years? Because my feed is like maybe 50% AI, something like crazy going on, or I see an AI-generated image. It's been like, I use trying to use social products from all around the world, and for a while I was using a social media app that was very popular in China. And the thing that struck me was that you had creators that were really good at AI-generated sort of fantastical architecture, and they had a real following even though their work was all generated, because they had a voice. So I think that is the next piece that not a lot of people are doing well, which is yes, you can be using AI for generating videos or text, but if it's just generic or if it's just a bunch of random things that you manage to generate, I don't think that's going to generate following or a real presence on these platforms. Whereas, I remember there was a photographer, an early Instagram photographer, probably one of our first 10,000 users, and he took a photo of the same hill outside his window every day. And that was like a photographic practice that he had. And that was really cool because then his followers could see that he had a view of the world and a perspective. And I think the same thing needs to be true to succeed as a creator, even if you're using AI tools.

Yeah, that's fascinating. Let's talk about people who don't have entrepreneurial ambitions, but they're like, I want to work for a company. Your hiring strategy at Anthropic has changed recently, right? You're hiring more high-level people. Is that right?

It's kind of a shift. So the way I think about it is you want people that are going to be defined more about the problems that they want to solve and how they can creatively solve them than a very specific sort of 'I know JavaScript and I'm going to do work in this exact environment.' And so I'm still really drawn to the folks that on the weekends or in their spare time are prototyping ideas. They came up with something, they're bringing that even to the interview process. You know, some of our product managers that we've talked to have had a culture of experimentation that they've been working through. And I think that's very interesting. I really look for that when I'm hiring. Interesting thing is it's not so different than when I was hiring for Instagram. The people I always gravitated towards were ones that, if you talk to them on a Monday morning, they'll tell you all about the new thing that they got interested in. It doesn't have to even be tech-related, but there is that sort of curiosity.
Excitement.
Exactly.

And I still absolutely look for that as well. And then in terms of the makeup of the teams that we want to build, you know, we haven't had a summer internship program. So we've tended less to hire fresh college grads, but I've been talking to a lot of people who are maybe going through college now or are recent graduates. You know, they're also enabling themselves via AI to sort of understand the market, understand the dynamics, be entrepreneurial in their own way, even if they're not starting their own companies, and then coming into companies and telling that story.
turns.zh: 而且我依然在寻找这一点。然后在我们要组建的团队构成方面，你知道，我们还没有暑期实习项目。所以我们不太倾向于招聘刚毕业的大学生，但我一直在和很多现在正在上大学或刚毕业的人交流。你知道，他们也通过 AI 来让自己理解市场、理解动态，以他们自己的方式保持创业精神，即使他们没有创办自己的公司，然后进入公司讲述那个故事。

turns.en: How do you learn that? How do you learn how to become entrepreneurial or generate ideas? Are you teaching your kids that?
turns.zh: 你是怎么学会这些的？你是怎么学会如何变得有创业精神或产生想法的？你在教你的孩子这些吗？

turns.en: Well, I mean, our kids are pretty young. I do try to encourage the idea of like observe the world and be open to what is there. You know, the thing I did early on was I had a little notebook that I would carry around everywhere and basically just always kind of writing and ideating, and like making space for that sort of quiet ideation time is really useful. One of the ways I've seen people use Claude, you know, if you ask Claude for one idea, it'll generate an idea. Maybe it'll be a good one. But the thing that's unique about it is it can also generate 50 or 100 ideas. So a practice that I find useful is give it five or ten and then ask it to fill in the next 30, and maybe one of those sparks something else. There's a lot of research where asking people to brainstorm together in a room is not as effective as asking one person to write down 10 ideas and pass those 10 ideas to the next person, have them generate the next 10. So you can simulate that same process but with AI.
turns.zh: 嗯，我是说，我们的孩子还很小。我确实试着鼓励他们观察世界，对周围的事物保持开放。你知道，我早期做的一件事是有一个小笔记本，我随身携带，基本上总是在写、在构思，为那种安静的构思时间留出空间，这真的很有用。我见过人们使用 Claude 的一种方式，你知道，如果你向 Claude 要一个想法，它会生成一个想法。也许那会是个好主意。但它的独特之处在于它还能生成 50 或 100 个想法。所以我发现一个有用的做法是给它五到十个，然后让它填补接下来的 30 个，也许其中一个会激发其他东西。有很多研究表明，让一群人聚在房间里头脑风暴，不如让一个人写下 10 个想法，然后把那 10 个想法传给下一个人，让他们生成接下来的 10 个。你可以用 AI 模拟同样的过程。

turns.en: Now, what is your ritual for generating ideas? You said quiet time. Do you go on a walk?
turns.zh: 那么，你产生想法的仪式是什么？你提到了安静的时间。你会去散步吗？

turns.en: Walks are really helpful for me. I also just like any kind of repeated action. I really like, like I got one of those Peloton rowing machines, and I found something. You're like, okay, it's a very repetitive action, but then your mind can kind of start wandering and start thinking about those different things. And also, you need to give your brain the opportunity to make new connections while you're not focusing on it, and then maybe later it'll come and say, oh yeah, that actually does connect really well.
turns.zh: 散步对我来说真的很有帮助。我也喜欢任何重复性的动作。我真的很喜欢，比如我买了一台 Peloton 划船机，我发现了一些东西。你会想，好吧，这是一个非常重复的动作，但然后你的思绪可以开始游荡，开始思考那些不同的事情。而且，你需要给你的大脑机会，在你没有专注的时候建立新的连接，然后也许稍后它会回来说，哦，是的，那实际上连接得非常好。

turns.en: Is it like every day that you make time for this?
turns.zh: 你是每天都为此腾出时间吗？

turns.en: I wish it were every day. It's more probably like once or twice a week these days, but I always, every time I do it, I'm like, I really should be doing this more regularly, and all of a sudden be excited to sit down and put pen to paper and then share that with the team.
turns.zh: 我希望是每天。这些天可能大概一周一两次，但我总是，每次做的时候，我都会想，我真的应该更规律地做这件事，然后突然就兴奋地坐下来，把笔落在纸上，然后和团队分享。

turns.en: What about going back to kids? I have two small kids, and sometimes I read these articles where, oh, people who just graduated from college are struggling to find jobs because a lot of entry-level jobs are being replaced with AI, and I'm like, okay, I'm worrying about myself, but now I have to worry about them as well. What are you teaching your kids? What do you think they're going to do in 10 years when they go out to the job market?
turns.zh: 回到孩子的话题呢？我有两个小孩，有时我读到这些文章，哦，刚大学毕业的人正在努力找工作，因为很多入门级工作被 AI 取代了，我就想，好吧，我在担心自己，但现在我还得担心他们。你在教你的孩子什么？你觉得他们 10 年后进入就业市场时会做什么？

turns.en: Yeah, it's super hard to predict what that market looks like, right, for a six- and a four-year-old. So the what might change a lot, and even some of the how will change, but I think there are a few things that are worth calling out. One is, talked a little bit before about being curious and observant about the world. That remains really powerful. They did this whole school event at my kids' school around even having the kindergarteners observe what could be better about the school and then create posters about ideas about how to improve them. That's a great mental exercise for kids.
turns.zh: 是的，很难预测那个市场会是什么样子，对吧，对于一个六岁和一个四岁的孩子来说。所以“什么”可能会改变很多，甚至一些“如何”也会改变，但我认为有几件事值得指出。一是，之前谈到过对世界保持好奇和观察。这仍然非常强大。他们在我孩子的学校举办了整个学校活动，甚至让幼儿园的孩子观察学校哪些地方可以更好，然后制作关于如何改进的想法海报。这对孩子来说是一个很好的思维练习。

turns.en: And like to even ask that question, you know, and some of the ideas are creative and some of them are kind of silly, but even having that mentality is something I think will serve anybody well as they grow up, because that's a change that you could try to make within your school or your community or your company, and so forth. So I think that piece matters.
turns.zh: 而且甚至要问那个问题，你知道，有些想法很有创意，有些则有点傻，但即使拥有那种心态，我认为随着他们长大，对任何人都有好处，因为那是你可以在学校、社区或公司里尝试做出的改变，等等。所以我认为这部分很重要。

turns.en: And I think the other one that should remain constant, like there was a lot of energy around learn to code, everybody should learn to code, and I think too many people interpreted that as you should learn Python, and it's like, yes, you can learn Python, that's going to be helpful for some things, but more than that, it's can you think in terms of systems, can you think systematically, and the folks that internalized that, I think, even with the advent of AI generating code, you can still apply those same techniques, were the ones that were just, oh yeah, I learned to code and now I'm feeling adrift because of that. So I think what I hope to encourage in my kids is that sense of curiosity and observation, and also this ability to think in terms of systems, like how do these things interrelate? You know, whenever they got, because of all the politics and news, they were interested in tariffs, and my wife had a really wonderful sort of interactive example of how interdependent economies might interact, and you could see their gears kind of turning. So that kind of like, explain the system, don't just explain the facts.
turns.zh: 而且我认为另一件应该保持不变的事情，比如有很多关于“学习编程”的热潮，每个人都应该学习编程，我认为太多人把它理解为你应该学习 Python，但实际上，是的，你可以学习 Python，那对某些事情会有帮助，但更重要的是，你能不能从系统的角度思考，你能不能系统地思考，而那些内化了这一点的人，我认为，即使 AI 生成了代码，你仍然可以应用那些相同的技术，而那些只是说“哦，是的，我学会了编程，现在我感觉漂泊不定”的人，正是因为那一点。所以我认为我希望鼓励我的孩子的是那种好奇心和观察力，以及这种从系统角度思考的能力，比如这些事情如何相互关联？你知道，每当他们因为所有的政治和新闻而对关税感兴趣时，我妻子有一个非常精彩的互动例子，展示相互依存的经济体如何互动，你可以看到他们的齿轮在转动。所以那就像是，解释系统，而不仅仅是解释事实。

turns.en: Love that. Can we talk a little bit about your English? Because I started my YouTube journey talking about English because I'm originally from Russia. I came with an accent, and then I learned how to speak like an American. You sound like an American. How did that happen?
turns.zh: 喜欢这个。我们能谈谈你的英语吗？因为我开始我的 YouTube 之旅时是谈英语的，因为我来自俄罗斯。我带着口音来，然后我学会了像美国人一样说话。你听起来像美国人。那是怎么发生的？

turns.en: I think it was a couple of things. One was I was interested in music from a very early age, and especially American and British bands. So I loved Oasis. Actually, going to go see them in a couple weeks. I'm excited. But I never saw them. Are they coming here? They're coming to Pasadena. So I'm going to play. But like, if you're singing in that language, you know, you have to kind of hear yourself for it to even rhyme or sound good. And so I think music was a big part of it as well. And then we moved around a bunch when I was a kid, and the one constant were international schools. So, starting from a fairly early age, I was bilingual. But only lived in the States when I turned 18. And so there were some words that I had never really said out loud because I just read them and then internalized them over here. But it is funny. I mean, we've had maybe this experience too, where now I've been here for a while, I'm a citizen here now, but will never feel fully like I'm from here because I grew up in Brazil, but when I go to Brazil, I don't feel fully there. So kind of from both and from neither.
turns.zh: 我认为有几件事。一是我很小的时候就对音乐感兴趣，尤其是美国和英国乐队。所以我喜欢 Oasis。实际上，几周后要去看他们。我很兴奋。但我从没见过他们。他们会来这里吗？他们会来帕萨迪纳。所以我要去。但是，如果你用那种语言唱歌，你知道，你必须听到自己，才能让它押韵或听起来好听。所以我认为音乐也是很大的一部分。然后我小时候搬了很多次家，唯一不变的是国际学校。所以，从很小的时候起，我就是双语的。但直到 18 岁才住在美国。所以有些词我从来没有大声说过，因为我只是读过，然后在这里内化了。但这很有趣。我的意思是，我们可能也有过这种经历，现在我已经在这里待了一段时间，我现在是这里的公民，但永远不会觉得自己完全来自这里，因为我在巴西长大，但当我回到巴西时，我也不觉得完全属于那里。所以既来自两者，又都不属于。

turns.en: Yeah, that's super cool. I wanted to ask for advice for all the immigrants who are watching. Do you think if you want to build a company in AI, does it make sense to move to Silicon Valley, or with AI does it matter where you are?
turns.zh: 是的，那太酷了。我想为所有正在观看的移民问个建议。如果你想在 AI 领域创业，你认为搬到硅谷有意义吗？还是说有了 AI，你在哪里就不重要了？

turns.en: I think the barrier to creating products has really, really shortened. Before, especially in Brazil when I was growing up there, there wasn't really a talent market of really good engineers. I mean, now there is much more because there have been generations of companies that have been created, but that might not be the case for every single city or every single country. AI can definitely help there as well. There's also such a broader set of information and content around what to look for in a co-founder, how do you think about that initial idea, how do you build from there, how do you market. And what I've been really excited about is, whenever I talk to, for example, Brazilian entrepreneurs where I'm from, who are understanding uniquely Brazilian problems or uniquely Brazilian opportunities around our unique payment systems, how the Brazilian economy works, like the public safety questions, and then applying AI or applying technology to those problems, I think there is a tremendous opportunity there. One of the things I get excited about is in the past, if you had an idea there, your only path would have been, well, I hope I can go fundraise from Silicon Valley VCs. I think there's much more of an opportunity to build that locally and then try to fundraise. You don't need funds to build an...
turns.zh: 我认为创造产品的门槛真的、真的缩短了。以前，尤其是在巴西，我成长的地方，并没有真正优秀的工程师人才市场。我的意思是，现在多多了，因为已经有好几代公司被创建出来，但可能不是每个城市或每个国家都这样。AI 肯定也能在这方面提供帮助。还有更广泛的信息和内容，关于寻找联合创始人时要注意什么，如何思考最初的想法，如何从那里构建，如何营销。而让我非常兴奋的是，每当我跟我来自巴西的企业家交谈时，他们理解巴西独特的问题或独特的机遇，围绕我们独特的支付系统、巴西经济如何运作、比如公共安全问题，然后把 AI 或技术应用到这些问题上，我认为那里有巨大的机会。让我兴奋的一点是，过去如果你在那里有一个想法，你唯一的路径就是，好吧，我希望我能从硅谷的风投那里筹到钱。我认为现在有更多的机会在当地构建，然后再尝试融资。你不需要资金来构建一个……

turns.en: You can at least get to that point where you've gotten something exciting.
turns.zh: 你至少可以到达那个你有了令人兴奋的东西的阶段。

turns.en: Wanted to wrap up the language part. Yeah. Do you think language learning is going to be replaced by AI?
turns.zh: 想结束语言部分。是的。你认为语言学习会被 AI 取代吗？

turns.en: I really think about this because I've been out of Brazil for long enough where all of the sort of colloquialism or slang has moved on and I just haven't lived there in a long time. So I've used, even though I'm fluent in Portuguese, I'll now use Claude and say, "Hey, I'm about to send this to somebody who's like my age, like do I sound old or do I sound out of date?" And he'll be like, "Well, you might want to use this kind of language instead or something, you know, kind of nuance there." I still think the value of learning the nuances of language is still important. You know, we went to Korea with a lot of the Anthropic team in March, and Claude is actually quite good at Korean. We heard from people on the ground that it's the best of the models at Korean, but even so, they said it still sounds like a really cool Korean that grew up in LA and then moved back. And I was like, that's nuance. Like, I'm not sure...
turns.zh: 我确实会思考这个问题，因为我离开巴西已经够久了，所有的口语或俚语都已经变了，而我很久没在那里生活了。所以我会用，尽管我葡萄牙语很流利，我现在会用 Claude 说：“嘿，我要把这个发给一个跟我同龄的人，我听起来是不是很老或者过时了？”它会说：“嗯，你可能想用这种语言代替，或者类似的东西，你知道，那种细微差别。”我仍然认为学习语言的细微差别是有价值的。你知道，我们三月份和很多 Anthropic 团队去了韩国，Claude 的韩语其实相当好。我们听到当地人说它是所有模型里韩语最好的，但即便如此，他们说它听起来还是像一个在洛杉矶长大然后搬回来的很酷的韩国人。我就想，这就是细微差别。我不确定……

turns.en: American vibes.
turns.zh: 美国范儿。

turns.en: Yeah. So how do we continue to push that as well? But we're definitely getting to the point where that sort of vision of you can be in a country and interact with...
turns.zh: 是的。那我们怎么继续推动这个呢？但我们肯定正在达到那个愿景，就是你可以在一个国家，然后和……互动。

turns.en: Yeah, AI is going to become natural at some point. And then do you think there's going to be a wearable that we're wearing and it just interacts for you, listens for you?
turns.zh: 是的，AI 在某个时候会变得自然。然后你认为会有一种可穿戴设备，我们戴着它，它替你互动、替你听吗？

turns.en: I think so, although there's also the value of having technology-free interactions. So I think there's always still going to be that appeal of, right, I actually learned this language, I'm going to go and be with somebody in full presence rather than feel like we're being intermediated by technology.
turns.zh: 我想是的，尽管也有无技术互动的价值。所以我认为那种吸引力永远存在，对吧，我实际上学会了这门语言，我要去和某人在一起，完全临在，而不是觉得我们被技术中介了。

turns.en: Uh, do you have any rituals? Any hard nos because you're a dad, you're a husband, but you're also a CPO at this huge company. Can you talk about your day-to-day?
turns.zh: 呃，你有什么仪式吗？有什么硬性禁止的事吗？因为你是一个父亲、一个丈夫，但也是这家大公司的 CPO。你能谈谈你的日常吗？

turns.en: Yeah, I really focus on the routines that anchor my day. For a long time I resisted being a morning person, but now I've just realized I'm like...
turns.zh: 是的，我非常专注于那些锚定我一天的例行公事。很长一段时间我抗拒成为早起的人，但现在我意识到我就像……

turns.en: In the US you have to. It's like 4 a.m. people everywhere.
turns.zh: 在美国你必须这样。到处都是凌晨 4 点起床的人。

turns.en: Yeah. And the kids, they're going to start school at 8:00, so you got to get up early. But we have breakfast together and we wake up early enough where we actually have time to dedicate to breakfast, and that ends up being like this really great morning ritual. Sometimes we'll also do longer dinners with the kids and get to download the day, but those are more unpredictable. Sometimes they're exhausted and they just want to get through it and go into bedtime. So breakfast is a more reliable opportunity to set intentions and think about the day. So we'll always anchor on that, and then we read to them every night. And that's been fun to see the evolution from reading your very simple board books to now picking up these stories, and then now our six-year-old can sort of start reading to our four-year-old, which is also very cute.
turns.zh: 是的。孩子们 8 点要开始上学，所以你得起早。但我们一起吃早餐，我们起得足够早，实际上有时间专门吃早餐，这最终成了非常棒的早晨仪式。有时我们也会和孩子们吃更长的晚餐，了解他们的一天，但那些更不可预测。有时他们筋疲力尽，只想熬过去然后睡觉。所以早餐是一个更可靠的机会来设定意图和思考一天。所以我们总是锚定在那上面，然后我们每晚给他们读书。看着从读非常简单的纸板书到现在的故事书，再到我们六岁的孩子能开始给我们四岁的孩子读书，这很有趣，也很可爱。

turns.en: Oh, that's the best. They can take care of themselves.
turns.zh: 哦，那是最好的。他们能自己照顾自己了。

turns.en: Yeah, it's kind of that. So I think those start and finish anchors are really valuable. So no matter what, even if later I'm going to have to pick back some project that I'm doing, really stopping and spending that time and anchoring either side of the day has been great.
turns.zh: 是的，有点像那样。所以我认为那些开始和结束的锚点非常有价值。所以无论如何，即使稍后我得重新捡起我正在做的某个项目，真正停下来花时间锚定一天的两端一直很棒。

turns.en: Anything around travel? Do you have to travel a lot?
turns.zh: 旅行方面呢？你经常旅行吗？

turns.en: The travel pieces I've tried to do? One that was a newer thing, and it's not even using very much AI, but I discovered Time Shifter this year and it's been like the biggest changer. Yeah, it's the jet lag thing. When we were in Vivate, actually where we met, I used that app going into that trip, and the rest of the team would laugh at me because I was like, "All right, everybody, stop drinking coffee. It's 3:00 in the afternoon, and start taking melatonin." But it really worked. So now I'm a real believer in that kind of piece.
turns.zh: 我试着做的旅行方面的事？有一件比较新的事，甚至没怎么用 AI，但我今年发现了 Time Shifter，它真是最大的改变者。是的，就是时差那个东西。我们在 Vivate 见面时，我在那次旅行中用了那个应用，团队其他人会笑我，因为我说：“好了，大家，别喝咖啡了。现在是下午 3 点，开始吃褪黑素。”但它真的有效。所以现在我是那种东西的真正信徒。

turns.en: Couple of final questions. Do you ever wake up at night and think like, "Oh my god, where the world is going with AI?" because you see all the headlines and all the things happening. Are you optimistic or pessimistic?
turns.zh: 最后几个问题。你会在夜里醒来想“天哪，世界在 AI 的浪潮中走向何方”吗？因为你看到所有头条新闻和正在发生的一切。你是乐观还是悲观？

turns.en: I'm generally optimistic, but I'm also maybe a cautious optimism. It's optimism if you believe you can actually help steer things towards a good outcome. So one of the biggest things I want to do coming out of the Artifact experience, I knew I wanted to go work at a frontier model lab.
turns.zh: 我总体上是乐观的，但也许也是谨慎的乐观。如果你相信你实际上能帮助把事物引向好的结果，那就是乐观。所以从 Artifact 经历中走出来，我想做的最重要的事情之一，就是我知道我想去前沿模型实验室工作。

turns.en: I thought that that's where I was going to have the maximum impact in the next few years, but I really wanted to be somewhere where I felt aligned with the founding team and the core ethics of the company around how they thought about scaling AI. It's not just about building the most powerful AI you possibly can; it's also about dedicating effort to understanding how these models work, how we can control them, and how we can responsibly scale them. There are definitely conversations, both inside and outside Anthropic, about how this could be really positive for humanity, but it could also go quite badly. There will be economic impacts, labor impacts, and models we don't understand yet in terms of how they scale. So I wanted to be somewhere where we were also asking and working on those questions alongside the more purely 'let's just make the models really good' approach.
turns.zh: 我以为那是我未来几年能产生最大影响的地方，但我真的想去一个与创始团队和公司关于 Scaling（规模扩张）AI 的核心伦理观一致的地方。这不仅仅是尽可能构建最强大的 AI，还要投入精力去理解这些模型如何运作、我们如何控制它们，以及如何负责任地扩展它们。在 Anthropic 内外，肯定有很多讨论，认为这可能对人类非常有益，但也可能变得相当糟糕。会有经济影响、劳动力影响，以及我们还不了解其扩展方式的模型。所以我想去一个地方，在那里我们也在提出并研究这些问题，而不仅仅是纯粹的“让我们把模型做得更好”的方法。

turns.en: So do you think we're going to have universal basic income at some stage? And would companies like Anthropic sponsor it?
turns.zh: 那么你认为我们会在某个阶段实现全民基本收入吗？像 Anthropic 这样的公司会资助它吗？

turns.en: Yeah, I think how we help society navigate is very much an open question. The big open question we'll also have to tackle is: where do people draw meaning from in a place where not everybody has to work anymore? What is the source of both meaning and challenges? Is it finding ways in which people stay engaged? Is it that a lot of people will be entrepreneurial? As you mentioned, not everybody is going to have that kind of drive. So for those folks, what is the community they find? What is their personal challenge that retains that meaning?
turns.zh: 是的，我认为我们如何帮助社会应对这个问题非常开放。我们还需要解决的一个重大开放问题是：在一个不是每个人都必须工作的世界里，人们从哪里获得意义？意义和挑战的来源是什么？是找到让人们保持参与的方式吗？还是很多人会去创业？正如你提到的，不是每个人都有那种驱动力。那么对于这些人来说，他们找到的社区是什么？他们找到的、能保留那种意义的个人挑战是什么？

turns.en: What do you think?
turns.zh: 你怎么看？

turns.en: I think I look to sports as an interesting example where we draw a lot of meaning and high stakes from an environment that is actually completely fabricated. Not everything should be exactly like sports, but whether it's who's contributing the most to their city or their community, or who's mastered a particular thing, or even artistic pursuits like getting really into art or music, I find inspiration in those fields. Maybe more people will draw meaning from those kinds of pursuits where the yardstick is not necessarily how much money you made or whether your company is at the top of the leaderboard, but more around having a personal yardstick that you're working towards.
turns.zh: 我认为体育是一个有趣的例子，我们从一个完全虚构的环境中汲取了很多意义和高风险。不是所有事情都应该完全像体育，但无论是谁为城市或社区贡献最多，还是谁掌握了某件事，甚至是艺术追求，比如深入研究艺术或音乐，我在这些领域找到了灵感。也许更多人会从这些追求中获得意义，其中的衡量标准不一定是赚了多少钱或你的公司是否在排行榜上名列前茅，而是你有一个个人目标在努力实现。

turns.en: A hobby, like that sounds like a dream life, right? When you can just focus on your hobby and have all the basics.
turns.zh: 一个爱好，听起来像是梦想中的生活，对吧？当你只需要专注于爱好，基本生活都有保障。

turns.en: And if there's enough challenge or meaning in there to still matter.
turns.zh: 而且如果其中有足够的挑战或意义，仍然很重要。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: What are your top three favorite AI apps?
turns.zh: 你最喜欢的三款 AI 应用是什么？

turns.en: That's a good question. Of course, Claude Code. I spend a lot of time coding in Claude Code. One interesting one I've been using for a long time: I would log my meals, macros, and protein. It was always such a huge annoyance where you're estimating portion sizes. All these years of computer vision research, I think, just got completely taken over by feeding them into an LLM. So I've been using an AI-powered meal tracking app that does such a good job—you just take a photo and go back to your life.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。当然，Claude Code。我花了很多时间在 Claude Code 里编码。还有一个我用了很久的有趣应用：我会记录我的餐食、宏量营养素和蛋白质。以前总是很麻烦，要估算份量。我觉得这些年的计算机视觉研究，完全被喂给 LLM 取代了。所以我一直在用一款 AI 驱动的饮食追踪应用，它做得非常好——你只需拍张照片，然后回到你的生活。

turns.en: It has all your proteins and everything.
turns.zh: 它有你所有的蛋白质等等。

turns.en: And it's amazing. It estimates your portion sizes, etc. But what I love is it's actually a technology that hopefully makes me healthier, but also just helps me stay present—I'm not spending an extra five minutes on my phone finding the thing. I can just take a photo, move on, and go from there. And then last but not least, I also like anything that has to do with learning, like AI-powered learning. I've been enjoying both my kids using Duolingo ABC now to learn the alphabet, but also seeing what they've been doing, for example, in advancing language learning. So anything that brings in that AI-powered conversational piece. Within Claude, we launched Learning Mode recently, to not just give people answers but help people understand and learn and iterate from there.
turns.zh: 而且它很棒。它会估算你的份量等等。但我喜欢的是，它实际上是一种有望让我更健康的技术，同时也帮助我保持专注——我不需要额外花五分钟在手机上找东西。我可以拍张照片，继续前进，然后从那里开始。最后但同样重要的是，我也喜欢任何与学习有关的东西，比如 AI 驱动的学习。我一直很喜欢我的两个孩子用 Duolingo ABC 学习字母表，也看到他们在语言学习方面的进步。所以任何带来那种 AI 驱动的对话式体验的东西。在 Claude 中，我们最近推出了学习模式，不仅给人们答案，还帮助人们理解和学习，并从中迭代。

turns.en: Thank you so much, Michael. Very inspiring. Thank you.
turns.zh: 非常感谢，Michael。非常鼓舞人心。谢谢。

consensus.en: AI enables small teams to scale and maintain conceptual integrity, making solo or duo entrepreneurship more viable.
consensus.zh: AI 使小团队能够扩展并保持概念完整性，使单人或双人创业更加可行。

consensus.en: Entrepreneurs should build for future model capabilities, not current limitations, to leverage rapid AI progress.
consensus.zh: 创业者应为未来的模型能力而构建，而非当前限制，以利用 AI 的快速发展。

consensus.en: Domain expertise and customer understanding remain key differentiators even as AI lowers barriers to building.
consensus.zh: 即使 AI 降低了构建门槛，领域专业知识和客户理解仍是关键差异化因素。

consensus.en: AI will evolve from assistant to collaborator to autonomous co-worker, with humans verifying and validating.
consensus.zh: AI 将从助手演变为协作者，再到自主的同事，人类负责验证和确认。

consensus.en: Curiosity, observation, and systems thinking are essential skills for future generations, more than coding.
consensus.zh: 好奇心、观察力和系统思维是未来世代的基本技能，比编程更重要。

contrarian.en: Non-technical founders can now build prototypes with AI, democratizing entrepreneurship beyond engineers.
contrarian.zh: 非技术创始人现在可以用 AI 构建原型，使创业不再局限于工程师。

contrarian.en: AI-generated content needs a human voice and perspective to build a following, not just generic output.
contrarian.zh: AI 生成的内容需要人类的视角和声音来建立粉丝群，而不仅仅是通用输出。

contrarian.en: The ideal company size may shrink to one to five people with AI, challenging traditional venture funding models.
contrarian.zh: 理想的公司规模可能因 AI 缩小到 1-5 人，挑战传统的风险投资模式。

contrarian.en: AI can simulate effective brainstorming by generating many ideas, outperforming group sessions.
contrarian.zh: AI 可以通过生成大量想法来模拟有效的头脑风暴，胜过小组讨论。

contrarian.en: Language learning remains valuable for nuance and presence, even as AI translation improves.
contrarian.zh: 即使 AI 翻译不断改进，语言学习对于理解细微差别和保持临场感仍然重要。
